flood_zone.title: 100-year storm flood risk zone
flood_zone.note: the SFPUC's official 100-year storm flood risk zone, from DataSF. It models a very rare storm and covers storm runoff only, not bay or ocean flooding. Use it to see which blocks sit low.
flood_zone.popup: The SFPUC says areas inside this boundary are highly likely to see deep, connected flooding in a 100-year storm. It covers storm runoff only, not bay or ocean flooding, and a normal storm is far smaller.

past_storms_note: Coverage started in the Mission and is thinner elsewhere. Know a spot that floods? Use Report water during a storm.
rain_notes_title: How to read this for 1 to 2 inches of rain

rain_notes.text: The Dec 31, 2022 flood on 14th St came on a day with 5.46 inches, the second-wettest day on record in San Francisco. That is roughly three to five times a 1 to 2 inch storm.
Rain per hour matters more than the total. In December 2019, much of the rain came down in about an hour.
Smaller storms have mostly meant ponding. After a storm that gave many areas an inch or more, public works dealt with about 15 flooded areas, mainly intersections.

The map makers' reading, not a forecast: steady rain over many hours means ponding in the red areas. A burst of an inch or more in an hour, or clogged drains, is when the New Year's Eve 2022 pattern repeats.
